## 1. Executive Summary

Dump Trade is a web platform that lets individuals, businesses, and industries post materials
they no longer need, so that others who could use them can claim them instead of the items
being dumped, burned, or landfilled. The platform serves two overlapping needs:

- **Household/community reuse** — people give away or find usable items nearby.
- **Industrial/commercial symbiosis** — one business's waste (offcuts, byproducts, packaging,
  organic waste, etc.) becomes another's raw material.

The core value proposition: **make it as easy to give away or claim waste as it is to post
a photo on social media.**

## 2. Problem Statement

- Households and businesses generate waste that still has value but ends up dumped or burned
  due to lack of an easy redistribution channel.
- Open burning and illegal dumping are common where formal waste collection is expensive,
  slow, or unavailable.
- Small industries and workshops that could reuse offcuts, organic waste, or byproducts from
  other businesses often have no visibility into what's available nearby.

## 3. Solution Overview

A simple listing-and-claim marketplace:

1. **Post** — a user lists an item/material with a title, category, photo, quantity, and location.
2. **Browse/Search** — other users filter by category and location to find what they need.
3. **Claim** — a claimant requests the item; the poster is notified and contact info is shared.
4. **Collect & Close** — the listing is marked collected, closing the loop and feeding impact
   metrics (e.g. items reused, estimated kg diverted from landfill).

### Core MVP Features
- Register/login (individual or organization account type)
- Post a listing (title, category, photo, quantity/condition, location)
- Browse listings with category + location filters
- Claim a listing (status: available -> claimed -> collected)
- Basic notifications (in-app or email) on claim
- Simple impact counter (items reused / estimated waste diverted)

### Stretch Features (if time allows)
- Map view of nearby listings
- Recurring/bulk listings for organizations
- Trust badges (successful claim count)
- Report/flag listing
- Admin moderation view

## 5. Suggested Tech Stack

Pick based on team familiarity — speed matters more than novelty in a hackathon.

- **Frontend:** React + Vite + Tailwind CSS (fast to build, familiar to most teams)
- **Backend:** Go (net/http or a light framework) or Node/Express — whichever the team is
  fastest with
- **Database:** SQLite (Turso) or Postgres — SQLite is fastest to set up for a hackathon
- **Auth:** Email/password or single OAuth provider (Google) — avoid multi-provider auth for MVP
- **Image storage:** Simple object storage (e.g. Cloudinary free tier) or base64 in early MVP
- **Deployment:** Render or Vercel for frontend, Render for backend
- **Notifications:** In-app status only for MVP; email (Resend) if time allows

## 6. Project Structure (proposed)

```
dumptrade/
├── frontend/
│   ├── index.html           # Landing page
│   ├── browse.html          # Browse/search page
│   ├── listing.html         # Listing detail page
│   ├── post.html            # Post an item page
│   ├── login.html           # Login page
│   ├── register.html        # Register page
│   ├── css/
│   │   └── styles.css       # Shared design tokens + component styles
│   ├── js/
│   │   ├── api.js           # Fetch calls to the backend
│   │   ├── listings.js       # Rendering/filtering logic for cards
│   │   ├── claim.js          # Claim/collect button logic
│   │   └── auth.js           # Login/register form handling
│   └── assets/
│       └── icons/
├── backend/
│   ├── handlers/            # auth, listings, claims, users
│   ├── models/               # User, Listing, Claim
│   ├── db/                   # schema, migrations
│   ├── middleware/           # auth middleware
│   └── main.go / server.js
├── docs/
│   ├── wireframes/
│   └── pitch-deck/
└── README.md
```
Since there's no build step, each HTML page can pull in the same `css/styles.css` and only the
JS files it needs — keeps things simple for a 5-person team working in parallel without merge
conflicts in a bundler config.


## 7. Core Data Model (draft)

- **User**: id, name, email, password_hash, account_type (individual/organization), location
- **Listing**: id, user_id, title, category, description, photo_url, quantity, condition,
  status (available/claimed/collected), location, created_at
- **Claim**: id, listing_id, claimant_id, claimed_at, status

## 8. User Flow (MVP)

1. User registers/logs in
2. User posts a listing OR browses existing listings
3. Claimant filters by category/location, finds an item, claims it
4. Poster gets notified, contact details exchanged
5. Once collected, poster (or claimant) marks it as collected
6. Impact counter updates

## 9. Success Metrics for Demo

- Number of listings posted during demo/testing period
- Number of successful claims (full loop completed)
- Estimated waste diverted (simple weight/category-based estimate)
- Time-to-post and time-to-claim (showing how simple the flow is)

## 10. Open Questions / Brainstorm Notes

_Use this space to keep dropping ideas as the team discusses._

- Should industrial/organization accounts require any verification?
- Do we need in-app messaging, or is exchanging contact info enough for MVP?
- How do we estimate "kg diverted" without real weight data — self-reported estimate per category?
- What's the minimum viable notification system (poll on page load vs push/email)?
